fixes.explanation: Chief of the cupbearers is a real title in Pharaoh's court, friend. Genesis 40:2 mentions Pharaoh's chief cupbearer, but that's not Potiphar's job. Genesis 39:1 says he's captain of the guard. A guard captain handing out cups at the door would confuse everybody.

Walking out free would be a big change, friend, but that's not what verse 22 says. It says the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph's care, so Joseph is still in the prison, only now he's responsible for what's done there. And verse 23 tells us why the warden could relax: the LORD was with Joseph.

problems.problem: The passage does not say Pharaoh's palace has plenty of officers, and Genesis 40:2 does not establish that either.
Saying a free man would be a happy ending but 'we're not there yet' gives away that Joseph will eventually be freed.
